{"self_assessment": "Impact: I fetched a full 40-domino load for the shared bin early on, which kept the table supplied while the fish was going up. I laid the upper tail (stroke 3) onto the top line, so the fish has its tail fin on the upper side. In the final minutes I carried the start line on from its live end, curving it up to catch the top line, and that is what got the run catching from the start. Afterward about 88 of the 93 standing dominoes fell from the start, and the fish outline was complete.

Execution: I worked in steady batches of two or three dominoes, checking as I went. When the upper tail showed pale, I inspected the nose joint closely, worked out why it wasn't catching, and bridged it with a gentle curve. I inspected again once the nose was fixed. After that I kept my hands off the nose, as agreed, so nothing got bumped before the push.

Collaboration: I confirmed the plan out loud, worked alongside Priya on the nose, and stayed clear of other people's areas so we didn't bump each other. I kept my updates short and clear, and I backed the hands-off call near the end.

Leadership: I committed to my part early and delivered it, told the table where I was and what I was changing, and helped steer us to a clean, stable finish rather than risky last-minute tinkering. I helped the table reach a good result: a clear fish outline that was almost entirely connected to the start.", "my_share_percent": 30}
